title: State feedback
equipment: Active magnetic-bearing training rig and loaded conveyor motor
physicalPurpose: Choose stable bearing dynamics from measured states and reconstruct an unmeasured conveyor-motor load without presenting an observer estimate as a sensor.
objective: Place closed-loop poles with measured-state feedback.

simplifications: The bearing model is local and omits coil electrical dynamics, magnetic-force nonlinearity, drive delay, mechanical contact, and backup-bearing dynamics.
The motor model omits shaft flexibility, nonlinear friction, encoder quantisation, and drive delay.
The motor load is a constant model state during each record; the mismatch record changes true speed damping without changing the observer model.
Motor load truth is exposed only for Simulation validation and is not read by the Structured Text controller.
Simulation evidence does not qualify a physical bearing or conveyor drive.

baseline.limitation: Position-only bearing feedback does not settle, and a motor controller that assumes zero load retains speed error.

change.decision: Accept the nominal gains only after executed mode, estimation, limit, and mismatch evidence agrees with the reviewed model.

disturbances: Compare position-only and measured-state bearing recovery from the same +0.1 mm initial displacement.
Check a +0.1 mm bearing reference from centred conditions.
Compare zero-load assumption, nominal observer, and damping-mismatch observer motor records at 1 rad/s and 0.5 N m true load.

acceptance.window: first 12 seconds with a 2-second displacement-and-velocity settling hold
final 2 seconds after settling eligibility passes
final 5 seconds of the 20-second zero-load-assumption record
final 5 seconds of the 20-second nominal-observer record
final 5 seconds against Simulation truth after estimation eligibility passes
final 5 seconds of the damping-mismatch record

abortPredicates: Any required signal is nonfinite, stale, forced, invalid, missing, or bound to the wrong bench.
Bearing displacement, velocity, requested current, or applied current leaves the reviewed range.
Motor speed, requested torque, applied torque, estimate, or innovation leaves the reviewed range.
A compared record changes an undeclared model, gain, interval, initial state, limit, seed, or evidence class.
Simulation truth motor load is used by the controller or presented as an installed physical sensor.
safety.restorationMode: Disable each controller, verify applied current and torque are exactly zero, then reset the Simulation state before the next independent record.
safety.physicalApprovalRole: authorised controls engineer with the responsible rotating-equipment, electrical-safety, and machine-safety owners
simulationOnlyRestrictions: Motor load truth is a Simulation validation channel, not an installed torque sensor.
Zero coil current does not levitate a physical rotor; independent touchdown containment remains mandatory.
No physical bearing, coil drive, conveyor, or motor is operated.
Physical use requires reviewed topology, scaling, mechanical containment, current and overspeed protection, abort/restoration, and explicit immediate approval.

video.viewerOutcome: Place magnetic-bearing modes, reconstruct motor load, and explain why an observer estimate remains model-dependent.

learning.context: An active bearing needs displacement and velocity feedback, while a conveyor motor has encoder speed but no installed load-torque sensor.
learning.reason: Structural feasibility does not choose closed-loop modes, and a later motor load state is observable but unmeasured.
theory: State feedback places model modes by weighting each measured state.
Reference gain preserves the requested equilibrium for the reviewed feedback law.
An observer predicts model states and corrects them from measured-output innovation.
The separation principle is nominal and does not make an observer estimate physical truth.
learning.workedPrediction: Position-only bearing feedback has poles plus and minus j; K=[16,7] places poles at -3 and -4 with reference gain 12; L=[8,-20] places observer-error poles at -4 and -5; nominal load observation changes predicted motor equilibrium from 0.8333 to 1.0000 rad/s.
practicalPreparation: Verify Simulation evidence, both bench identities, states, estimates, truth-channel labels, requested/applied outputs, interval, limits, and disabled zero-output behavior.
Calculate and review every gain and pole before applying it to the executable model.
learning.baseline: Run position-only bearing feedback and the motor controller with a zero-load assumption.
learning.change: Use measured bearing state feedback and the nominal speed/load observer without changing the declared plants or limits.
learning.comparison: Compare equivalent bearing records and then zero-load, nominal-observer, and damping-mismatch motor records with predeclared eligibility and effort measures.
learning.validation: Accept nominal mode and estimation claims only when independent calculations agree with synchronized executable state, estimate, innovation, and constraint evidence.
learning.explanation: Velocity feedback supplies bearing damping; motor innovation reconstructs the nominal load state, while unmodelled damping is absorbed into an effective load estimate.
